items.heading: Agriculture Is a Real, Structurally
items.text: Agriculture is a real, structurally growing field in India, but "is agriculture good" is really three or four different questions wearing one coat. A government ICAR scientist, an agribusiness manager at an FMCG company, an agritech product manager, and a farmer cultivating two acres of wheat are all "in agriculture." Their income structure, risk, and daily work have almost nothing in common.

items.heading: Before Comparing Pay Tables
items.text: Before comparing pay tables or exam routes, get this distinction straight, because it changes which section of actually applies to you.

items.heading: Most Degree
items.text: Most degree-holder agriculture careers in India start with a 4-year BSc Agriculture (Honours), earned either through the ICAR All India Entrance Examination for Admission (AIEEA UG), which reserves a share of seats across ICAR-linked and state agricultural universities nationally, or through a specific state's own CET route into its state agricultural university.

items.heading: Owning or Working Family Land
items.text: Owning or working family land as the main livelihood means your income depends on rainfall, soil, crop prices at harvest time, and how much of your produce actually sells at MSP (Minimum Support Price) versus the open market, most Indian farmers sell most crops in the open market, not at MSP.
